annotations: OWNER-DECISIONS 197, verbatim: 197. DC records of 20 mph on Canal Rd NW (block dc-4633425-0) and the Whitehurst Fwy (dc-4636053-0), owner 2026-10-02: "Override: keep LTS 4 (Recommended)". A stress override holds them at the OSM speeds and LTS 4, and they stay listed in the discrepancy report. Implemented as a block-level exclusion rather than stress rows: the two blocks' posted speed is withheld from the overlay (`routemaker.agency_roads.withheld_blocks`), so OSM's posted 35 mph stands on every way matched to them and the tier follows from it by the same tables as every other road (LTS 4). A stress row would have held the tier while the classifier still read DC's 20 mph, and would have been keyed to way ids that change when OSM splits a way. Each block is named by DC's own key for it, BLOCKKEY, with its ROUTENAME as a check a reader can see; the block ids in the quote (dc-<OBJECTID>-<part>) are the installed ids of 2026-10-01, built from the ArcGIS row number, which DC's republishing may reassign, so they are not what the rebuild matches. A key that names no installed block, or another street, withholds nothing and the rebuild's log warns of it. Everything else the blocks record (lanes, one-way, count) still applies. The discrepancy report lists the ways under posted speed, not applied, reason "owner override". The ways named below are those matched to the blocks on the Geofabrik extract of 2026-09-24, for the reader; the rebuild matches afresh.
